content: The data presented reflects the outcomes of HPV testing and follow-up at various intervals, comparing results to baseline scenarios and no screening scenarios. Below is a detailed interpretation of the findings: 1. Baseline HPV Testing at 12 Months: The number of HPV cases was 1,290, representing a 34% reduction compared to no screening. The difference from the baseline scenario was a decrease of 18 cases (1% reduction). Precancer treatment cases were 915, showing a 37% reduction compared to no screening, with a difference of 14 fewer cases (1% reduction) from the baseline. The cost associated with this scenario was 13,025, which was an increase of 627 (5% higher) compared to no screening. The number needed to treat (NNT) was 24, an increase of 1 (2% higher). Deaths were 25, an increase of 2 (7% higher). 2. Post-Treatment Follow-Up: HPV Testing at 24 Months: HPV cases increased to 1,337, a 31% reduction compared to no screening, with a difference of 28 additional cases (1% increase) from the baseline. Precancer treatment cases rose to 949, a 35% reduction compared to no screening, with 21 additional cases (1% increase) from the baseline. The cost decreased to 12,186, which was 212 lower (2% reduction) compared to no screening. The NNT remained at 24, an increase of 1 (2% higher). Deaths decreased to 23, with no change (2% reduction) compared to the baseline. 3. HPV and Cytology Triage at Baseline (12 Months): HPV cases were 1,329, a 32% reduction compared to no screening. Precancer treatment cases were 947, a 35% reduction compared to no screening. The cost was 8,693, with an NNT of 17 and deaths at 25. 4. Post-Treatment Follow-Up: Co-Testing at 12 Months: HPV cases were 1,309, a 33% reduction compared to no screening, with a difference of 20 fewer cases (1% reduction) from the baseline. Precancer treatment cases were 932, a 36% reduction compared to no screening, with 15 fewer cases (1% reduction) from the baseline. The cost increased to 9,388, which was 695 higher (8% increase) compared to no screening. The NNT was 18, an increase of 1 (5% higher). Deaths were 26, an increase of 1 (6% higher). 5. Post-Treatment Follow-Up: HPV Testing at 24 Months: HPV cases increased to 1,358, a 30% reduction compared to no screening, with a difference of 30 additional cases (2% increase) from the baseline. Precancer treatment cases rose to 969, a 33% reduction compared to no screening, with 22 additional cases (2% increase) from the baseline. The cost decreased to 8,497, which was 195 lower (2% reduction) compared to no screening. The NNT remained at 17, with no change (2% increase). Deaths decreased to 24, with no change (1% reduction) compared to the baseline. The percentages in brackets represent the change relative to no screening for cervical cancer cases and deaths. For precancer treatment, NNT, and cost, the percentages indicate the difference compared to the baseline scenario for the respective flowchart.
